newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called higher amid storm fears, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called higher amid storm fears, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Thursday amid concerns over a tropical depression brewing in the Gulf of Mexico and firmer cash prices, market sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.225 to $2.235 after settling to the upside at $2.174 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August last traded 3.4 cents firmer at $2.208.
The tropical depression, packing maximum sustained winds of about 35 miles per hour, forced some crews to evacuate several offshore rigs as a precaution.

Texaco on Wednesday removed a dozen workers from offshore platforms and planned to evacuate another 50 on Thursday, and the U.S. Coast Guard received reports from crews shutting in platforms in the Eugene Island section of the Gulf.
Shipping was not affected, but the Coast Guard broadcast a warning of severe thunderstorms and strong winds.
In anticipation of the storm potentially being upgraded to a tropical storm, cash prices rose a few cents to about $2.27-2.28 at Henry Hub.
Also supporting cash and futures was the unrelenting heat across most of the U.S., but the near 100-degree temperatures were expected to subside in the Northeast and Midwest this weekend.
Chart traders still pegged August resistance at the down trendline at $2.23 and then at $2.29 and $2.36. Support was seen at $2.15 and then at last week's low of $2.051.

Separately, AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 87 bcf, the low end of average expectations in the 85-95 bcf range. Overall stocks are still 215 bcf, or 14 percent, over year ago.

Eastern inventories increased by 65 bcf and remained 76 bcf, or nine percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage gained six bcf last week but continued to lag 1996 levels by about seven percent. Stocks in the producing region were still 47 percent above last year.
